The tested turbine has four sets of blades, each consisting of two moving parts.
By changing the angle between the blade parts, the swept area of the turbine can be adjusted from 206 mm (for 30-degree angle) to 700 mm (for 180-degree angle).
The maximum torque of 4.8 Nm was achieved at a rotational speed of 20 rpm for the 100-degree blade angle.
The maximum power output of 40.5 W was reached at 100 rpm for the 180-degree blade angle.
The maximum aerodynamic efficiency of 0.082 was obtained for the 100-degree blade angle.
The computational mesh consisted of 2.8 million elements, with an average element quality of 0.76196.
The K-omega SST turbulence model was used in the CFD simulations.
The simulations were performed for wind speeds of 10 m/s and rotational speeds ranging from 20 rpm to 180 rpm.
The variable swept area design allows the turbine to adapt to different wind speeds and protect the rotor from damage in high-wind conditions.

The torque generated by a single blade during a rotation showed a sinusoidal pattern, with the highest torque occurring when the blade was positioned perpendicularly to the concave surface against the wind.
The power coefficient showed a non-linear trend, with the maximum value of 0.082 achieved at a rotational speed of 100 rpm for the 100-degree blade angle.
The turbine with a blade angle of 100 degrees had the highest torque coefficient, while the 180-degree angle had the maximum power output.
The torque and power output both showed a non-linear decrease as the rotational speed increased.
The blade geometry had a width of 250 mm, a thickness of 50 mm, and a distance of 350 mm from the axis of rotation.
The computational domain for the CFD simulations had a height (half) of 1000 mm, a length of 2700 mm, and a width of 1800 mm.
